summary: US equities had a mixed session on August 24, with the broad S&P 500 slipping 0.28% while the Dow Jones edged up 0.26% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.12% as technology stocks led the decline, dropping 2.01% on the day. Defensive sectors held up well, with Consumer Staples gaining 1.67% and Financials rising 1.23%, while the VIX climbed 4.76% to 21.29 reflecting a modest uptick in short term anxiety. The 10 year Treasury yield fell 0.72% suggesting bond prices rose as investors rotated toward safety, while gold was essentially flat at down 0.01% and Bitcoin gained 2.32%. Overseas markets were largely calm, with Canada up 0.26%, the UK up 0.35%, Japan up 0.33%, and Australia up 0.70%, while European and Hong Kong indices finished near flat. The CNN Fear and Greed Index held steady at 55 Neutral, unchanged from a week ago and up from 41 a month ago, suggesting sentiment has stabilized. The single most notable stock story was a broad selloff across AI and cloud related names including MongoDB down 6.5%, Micron down 5.8%, Super Micro down 5.6%, Cloudflare down 4.4%, and Robinhood down 4.2%, driven by a combination of analyst commentary and financing concerns in the AI cloud space. Looking ahead, Wednesday brings the preliminary GDP reading and the Core PCE inflation index, Thursday brings unemployment claims, and Friday features Fed Chairman Warsh speaking alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision and revised University of Michigan consumer sentiment.
